source.publication: 2025 AR1000F and AR1000NR Instructions (with the 2025 AR1000F return)
source.section: AR1000F lines 7A-7C, 8-25, 27-29, 34, 37-38 (Form pages 1-2); Instructions PDF page 12 LINE 7A (29 per taxpayer and spouse; 65 or over on January 1, 2026; 65 Special), PDF page 14 Standard Deduction table and LINES 26-29, PDF pages 30-34 Regular Income Tax Table (schedule 0% to 5,600, 2% to 11,200, 3% to 15,990, 3.4% to 26,400, 3.9% above, as settled in the record from the table), PDF page 11 item 8 (Social Security and Railroad Retirement exempt); PDF page 11 items 12 and 13 and the NOTE (total exemptions from all plans under 12 and 13 cannot exceed 6,000 per taxpayer); PDF page 13 LINE 18A and 18B (public or private employment-related plans, the recipient does not have to be retired; traditional IRA after 59 1/2); record ar_employer_plan_exclusion, ar_traditional_ira_exclusion_59_5; PDF page 13 LINE 16 (premature distributions); PDF page 14 LINE 32

worked: Joint, 58 and 62. Primary: wages 50,000 and a traditional IRA distribution 10,000 at 58 (premature, no death or disability). Spouse: traditional IRA 4,000 at 62. Only the spouse is over 59 1/2: the spouse's 4,000 is exempt (under the 6,000), the primary's 10,000 is taxable. Federal (given, not tested): federal AGI = wages (primary) 50,000.00 + traditional IRA distribution (primary) 10,000.00 + traditional IRA distribution (spouse) 4,000.00 = 64,000.00. Federal taxable income = 64,000.00 - standard deduction 31,500.00 = 32,500.00 (federal senior deduction ignored). AR1000F, filing status 2 (married filing joint); Arkansas builds its own income from lines 8-25, which here equals federal AGI less the exempt items. Line 8 wages 50,000.00. Line 16 premature traditional IRA distribution (primary, age 58, under 59 1/2) 10,000.00, taxable in full (no 6,000 exemption: PDF page 11 item 13, PDF page 13 LINE 18B). Line 18B (spouse, age 62): gross traditional IRA after 59 1/2 4,000.00 = 4,000.00; less the 6,000 exemption: exemption = lesser of 4,000.00 and 6,000.00 = 4,000.00; taxable 0.00. Line 23 total income = 60,000.00; line 24 adjustments 0.00; line 25 AGI = 60,000.00. Projection check: federal AGI 64,000.00 - 6,000 exclusion (ar_retirement_exclusion_59_5_plus) 4,000.00 = state AGI 60,000.00. Line 27 standard deduction (filing status 2) 4,940.00; line 28 net taxable income = 60,000.00 - 4,940.00 = 55,060.00. Line 29 tax, schedule as numbers (0% to 5,600): 2% x (11,200.00 - 5,600.00) 5,600.00 = 112.00 + 3% x (15,990.00 - 11,200.00) 4,790.00 = 143.70 + 3.4% x (26,400.00 - 15,990.00) 10,410.00 = 353.94 + 3.9% x (55,060.00 - 26,400.00) 28,660.00 = 1,117.74; total 1,727.38. (The Regular Income Tax Table row 55,001-55,101 gives 1,727; expected keeps the schedule.) Line 7A boxes: personal 2 = 2 x 29.00 = 58.00; line 7C and line 34 58.00; line 37 total credits 58.00. Line 38 net tax = 1,727.38 - 58.00 = 1,669.38. Line 32 (10% of the federal additional tax: 10% x 1,000.00 = 100.00) is not added by the projection (approximations). Status 4 is not lower here (the spouse has no taxable Arkansas income).
accepted_approximations: Arkansas builds its own income (AR1000F lines 8 to 25) instead of starting from federal AGI; the projection starts from federal AGI less taxable Social Security (exempt) and the reliefs here.

The schedule's bracket starts are derived from the printed tax table, which rounds the tax at each row's midpoint to the dollar; between rows and in rounding the projection's tax differs from the table.
The additional tax on early distributions (10% of the federal Form 5329 additional tax, line 32) is not added.
